problem: The lines $4x-8y=7$ and $3y-px=9$ are perpendicular. The value of $p=$
worked_solution:
For the two lines to be perpendicular, their slopes must multiply to $-1.$

To find the slope of $4x-8y=7,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-8y & =7 \\ -8y & =-4x+7 \\ 8y & =4x-7 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}x-\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of $3y-px=9,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}3y-px & =9 \\ 3y & =px+9 \\ y & =\frac{p}{3}x+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

- The slope of the line $4x-8y=7$ is $\frac{1}{2}.$

- The slope of the line $3y-px=9$ is $\frac{p}{3}.$

Multiplying the slopes together, we have

$$
\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{p}{3}=-1\,⟹\,p=-6.
$$
